The owner already holds 202.30 BPT from an earlier `Temp.s.sol` withdrawal, and phStaging2 will transfer it owner -> escrow explicitly." | story-052 L211-212 (Follow-ups): "the owner's pre-existing 202.30 BPT is transferred owner -> escrow explicitly ... be computed on the escrow's COMBINED BPT balance after the owner -> escrow transfer: the old pooler's BPT (~20,401.8 at planning time) plus the owner's 202.30" | story-052 L217: "The phStaging2:103 fork test must transfer the owner's actual mainnet BPT (202.30 at planning time) into the escrow" | story-103 L199: "Fork test: exercise the owner's real pre-existing mainnet BPT (202.30 at planning time; read the live balance) being transferred owner -> escrow, and compute `minAmountsOut` over the escrow's COMBINED BPT balance ... then assert `exitAndSeed` succeeds with those floors." | story-103 L201 and L224-225 (same COMBINED wording)
specSource: 052 Design step 2 + Follow-ups; 103 Checklist L199/L201 + amendment L224-225
description: The escrow code is correct and premise-independent: it exits `BPT.balanceOf(this)`. The stories, however, instruct work on a balance that does not exist. (a) story-103's L199 fork-test item cannot be satisfied as written, because there is no owner BPT to transfer, so the test either trivially transfers 0 or is quietly dropped. (b) Conditional on a future phStaging2:103 implementation that ignores the 'read the live balance' / 'read both live' qualifiers (052 L211-212; 103 L199, L201, L224-225): the 'COMBINED ... plus the owner's 202.30' wording invites floors sized on 20,604.11 BPT. Those exceed the true share by 0.99%, so exitAndSeed reverts AmountOutBelowMin at any tolerance below about 1%. That fails loud, before any wiring step, and loses no value. (c) Under the same condition, a hardcoded `transfer(escrow, 202.30e18)` from the owner would revert. The repeated 'read the live balance' / 'read both live' qualifiers make a correct implementation possible (a 0 transfer is a no-op), so the harm is wasted broadcasts and confusion, not loss. (d) Context for the human, outside escrow scope and not part of the severity basis: the tax/accounting rationale of story-052 (L23, 'never through the owner's EOA') was already not met for this 202.30 BPT tranche. Its exit proceeds (222.90 phUSD + ~130 USDC) landed on the owner EOA at block 25,985,119, and 103 L116 records three further Temp.s.sol withdrawals to other EOAs (150 / 200 / 1,847.77 BPT).
deviation: The story text asserts on-chain state ('The owner already holds 202.30 BPT') that was false when the story was written. Stories 052 and 103 must drop the owner -> escrow BPT transfer, or reduce it to an explicit live-read that is allowed to be zero and logs the zero. The L199 fork-test checklist item must be restated, and the floor sizing must use only the escrow's actual BPT balance (the old pooler's 20,401.809... BPT).
impact: Law-2 (faithfulness). The story asserts on-chain state that is false ('The owner already holds 202.30 BPT', 052 L59) and directs an acceptance criterion that cannot be satisfied (103 L199). That present defect is the severity basis. Conditional impacts, only if future phStaging2:103 code ignores the stories' 'read the live balance' qualifiers: floors sized on the combined 20,604.1 BPT exceed the true share by 0.99%, so exitAndSeed reverts at any tolerance below 0.99%, and a hardcoded transfer of 202.30e18 reverts. No value is lost (ECON-005). Point (d) (tax rationale) is context only. Low, because the false premise and unsatisfiable acceptance criterion on a pending mainnet runbook need story amendment before execution.
